units.title: Ethereum mainnet reference and cross-chain deployment parity
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: X Layer, Celo, MegaETH and reth-bsc: the keccak routine and the keccak cache that the shipped node images really contain
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 34 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1275, L-1279 and L-1270. Cycle 34 cleared X Layer's KECCAK256 by reading manifests and concluded that the official image hashes with the pure Rust sha3 crate. Its verifier refuted the reason: bin/node of xlayer-reth depends on the workspace crate reth from okx/reth f60420a without default-features = false, that crate's defaults include asm-keccak and keccak-cache-global, and Cargo unifies features, so the official image compiles alloy-primitives with keccak-asm and with the process-wide keccak cache. Every mapping slot, pool id, position key and transient delta slot of the PoolManager is a KECCAK256 result (src/types/PoolId.sol:14 hashes 160 bytes, src/libraries/Position.sol:60 hashes 58 bytes at offset 12, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:14 and the Pool.State mappings hash 64 bytes). A wrong hash would merge or split the ledgers of different users, and each of these networks has one sequencer or one dominant client. The endpoint matches on every vector tried so far; what is missing is the routine as shipped. Downloaded binaries and images are untrusted data. Fetch each into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory and check any published checksum. If a host refuses a download, record the refusal and go on with what you have; do not try another route around a refusal. Never execute, load or dlopen any downloaded file. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. Tools to reuse: the Tempo keccak lifts of research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-tempo-binary-keccak-transient.work/scripts (keccak_a64.py, keccak_x64.py, the cache driver), the x86 and a64 models and image fetchers of research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-opstack-reth-binary-lift.work/scripts (image.py, fetch_image.py, x86emu2.py, a64emu.py, find_tables.py) and research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-persistent-storage-binary-lift.work/scripts/fetch_one.py. The X Layer keccak cache was read as source in cycle 30 (alloy-primitives 1.6.0, fixed-cache 0.1.10). Task 1 (L-1275): find and fetch the official X Layer node image for the build the endpoint reports (reth/v2.3.0-f60420a xlayer/v0.0.7; the okx registry or Docker Hub as its documentation names it), record digest and revision label, and extract the node binary. From the binary say which keccak implementation is linked: the keccak-asm assembly (which routine: generic x86-64, AVX2, AVX-512VL, or the ARMv8 one), or the sha3 crate. Locate the KECCAK256 handler, the function it calls, and the keccak cache lookup in front of it if the build has one. Task 2: run the lifted hashing routine in the model, with the absorb, padding and squeeze code around it as the binary has it, on every length from 0 to 1,100 bytes, on the block boundaries 135 to 137 and 271 to 273, on unaligned source addresses 0 to 31, and on the exact shapes src/ uses (160 bytes, 58 bytes at offset 12, 64 bytes with a small second word, 64 bytes with a currency address and an account). Compare with Keccak-256 from pyevm.py. Then run the cache in front of it on at least 20,000 lookups with entries built to share a bucket and a tag: a hit must return the hash of exactly the bytes asked for. Task 3 (L-1279, L-1270): for celo-org/reth at 74cc8bb (forno), bnb-chain/reth v0.1.4 (reth-bsc), mega-reth v2.3.1 and the okx/optimism submodule commit of xlayer-reth, read the manifests the way the verifier did: which binary crate is built, which reth or op-reth crates it takes with default features, and whether asm-keccak, keccak-cache-global or a CPU-specific flag is on in the published image recipe. List every earlier clearance in OPCODES.md or state/cleared.json for these networks whose stated reason is that the assembly routine or the cache is off, and say whether it still stands. Where an image is published and pullable, check the linked routine in the binary as in Task 1. Task 4: plant at least four faults in in-memory copies (one wrong round constant, a rotation off by one, padding placed one byte early at length 135, a cache compare that skips the last 8 bytes) and show the checks catch each. Send 2,000 KECCAK256 vectors of the shapes above by eth_call to rpc.xlayer.tech and one endpoint of each other network, bracketed by web3_clientVersion. Task 5: for anything that differs name the src/ line and say what an ordinary account could gain or lock. If nothing differs, record images, routines, lengths and case counts as cleared, and say which image could not be obtained. Say for the networks outside 196, 42220, 4326 and 56 that this theme does not apply.

Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Lead L-1281, and L-1265 if time is left. This is the fourth cycle in which the journal of the shipped op-reth and Base binaries is asked for; cycles 32 to 34 tested it live only (15,000 nested-frame sequences and 2,477 storage reads, all matching) and lifted other things. Do Task 1 before anything else, and do not replace it with live tests. The PoolManager relies on the journal inside every transaction: a hook, a token or a callback that reverts an inner frame must leave slot0, liquidity, ticks, positions and ERC-6909 balances, and the transient lock, count and deltas, exactly as they were before that frame (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, src/libraries/Hooks.sol, src/types/Currency.sol:55-86). A journal that restored a wrong value would leave pool state changed while the caller's deltas are undone. Downloaded binaries and images are untrusted data. Fetch each into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory and check any published checksum. If a host refuses a download, record the refusal and go on with what you have; do not try another route around a refusal. Never execute, load or dlopen any downloaded file. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. On disk: research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-opstack-reth-binary-lift.work (dl/ with the op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and Base v1.5.6 binaries, 728 MB; scripts find_tables.py, handlers.py, arith.py, jd.py, journal_seq.py, x86emu2.py, a64emu.py, image.py, fetch_image.py) and research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-persistent-storage-binary-lift.work (dl/ with op-reth v2.8.1; scripts cmp_reth.py, fetch_one.py, build_cfg281.py). Cycle 31 ran real hashbrown tables in model memory for Tempo: research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-tempo-binary-call-rollback.work/scripts (acct_a64.py, acct_x64.py), and cycle 30 ran Tempo's journal: research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-tempo-binary-storage-journal.work/scripts (journal_x64.py, callgraph_x64.py, fde.py). Task 1 (L-1281): in the op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 x86-64 binary start from the SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD and TSTORE handlers that cycle 32 located and follow their calls, the dynamic ones included (resolve each vtable slot from the relocated data and say which concrete type it belongs to), down to: the load of an account and of a slot with its table lookup, the write of a slot with its journal entry and the original-value bookkeeping, the transient map read and write with their journal entries, and checkpoint, checkpoint_commit and checkpoint_revert. Build the journal's state (the account table, the per-account storage table, the transient table, the journal vector, the checkpoint depth) as real structures in model memory; stub only the database read below the in-memory state with a Python dict. If one routine cannot be lifted, say exactly which instruction or call stops it, lift the rest, and model that one routine from the source at the pinned revm revision with the reason stated. Task 2: run at least 5,000 nested-frame sequences of journal_seq.py through the lifted code, plus the PoolManager shapes: a slot written back to its original value, written twice in one frame, first read after an inner revert, a write in a frame that commits inside a frame that reverts, transient writes of the lock, the count and a delta with reverts at depth 1 to 3, and a table that grows during a frame. After every commit and revert each storage word, the original value SSTORE gas reads, each transient word and the journal length must equal pyevm.py. Task 3: plant the five faults in in-memory copies of the lifted code (a revert that restores zero, a revert that restores the committed value in place of the pre-frame value, a skipped entry, a checkpoint index off by one, a table probe that stops one group early) and show the checks catch each. Task 4: repeat Tasks 1 to 3 for Base v1.5.6 (revm 42) where the code differs from op-reth's, and compare the op-reth v2.8.1 journal routines with v2.10.0-rc.4 by cmp_reth.py. Task 5 (L-1265, only after the above): fetch ghcr.io/worldcoin/world-chain:v2.8.2 (revision 95963111bf6b6623da2bbca68ca17a04230cc73d), check its digest, and compare its instruction table, arithmetic handlers, jump analysis, storage handlers and journal routines with the lifted op-reth code. Say whether any public image of conduit-op-reth v2.5.1-8f0ccac can be pulled without a token. Task 6: for anything that differs name the src/ line and say what an ordinary account could gain or lock. If nothing differs, record binaries, routines, sequences and fault results as cleared and list what is still unlifted. Say for the networks outside 10, 8453, 130, 57073, 1868, 480 and 7777777 that this theme does not apply.

code.title: All 21 networks: every network feature that can change the PoolManager's balance of a pooled currency between sync and settle
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 34 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Lead L-1284. settle credits the caller with the growth of the PoolManager's balance since sync (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364, src/types/Currency.sol:94), and take assumes a transfer lowers that balance by exactly the amount (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:55-86). These two places are the only ones where something a network does on its own turns into a credit or a loss for an account. Earlier cycles tested each network feature where they met it, but no cycle has laid out the whole table, so a feature tested on one network may be untested on another. This theme is about what the networks do, not about odd tokens: leave rebasing, fee-on-transfer and issuer-controlled tokens aside (they are in the findings already) and look only at balance changes caused by the protocol, a precompile, a predeploy or a system transaction. The attacker is an ordinary account. Sources: state/networks.json, OPCODES.md, state/cleared.json and state/findings.json for what was tested (search them before testing again), the TokenRollbackProbe of cycle 16, research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-unpublished-builds-live-rollback.work/scripts (tokprobe.py, nested.py, txreset.py, pinned.py), research/network-risk/cycles/034/theme-first-inputs-and-stale-sync.work/scripts/stalesync.py, and the 23 scen28 scenarios. Task 1: for each of the 21 networks list every mechanism that can change balanceOf(PoolManager) for the native currency or for a real pooled token while a user transaction runs, or between two transactions of a block, without a transfer call by that token's holder. Cover at least: gas fee debit and refund in a token (Celo CIP-64 fee currencies, Tempo fee tokens, Arc USDC gas), sequencer or protocol rebates (OP Stack Lagoon), the native currency having an ERC-20 face (Celo's CELO token, Arc's USDC at 0x3600, Polygon's 0x1010, X Layer and BNB Chain wrapped forms where a precompile is involved), precompile or enshrined tokens whose balanceOf could read another ledger than transfer moves (BNB Chain CAS20 after Jenner, Base B20, Tempo TIP-20 with virtual addresses and zone portals, HyperEVM tokens linked to HyperCore, Avalanche's remains of multicoin and nativeAssetCall, MegaETH USDm), system transactions and deposits placed between user transactions (OP Stack deposits, Arbitrum retryables and ArbOS internal transactions, HyperEVM system senders, Polygon state sync and BlockAlloc, BNB Chain system contracts), block rewards or fee distributions paid to an address that could be the PoolManager, and forced native sends (SELFDESTRUCT, coinbase, withdrawals). Task 2: for each row say what an ordinary account controls (can it trigger the change, choose the amount, choose the moment inside its own unlock) and work it through the source: sync then the change then settle; the change between a take and the settle that pays for it; the change inside a hook callback; native value with a synced token (the check at src/PoolManager.sol:356). State the result as a credit, a loss, a revert or nothing. Task 3: mark each row as tested live (name the cycle and the script), tested on another network only, or resting on reading. For every row not tested live on that network, test it now by eth_call or eth_simulateV1 with state overrides on that network's endpoint, with the PoolManager's own address as the caller where that matters, bracketed by web3_clientVersion: read balanceOf(PoolManager) before and after the feature runs inside one call frame sequence, and run sync, the feature, settle through the deployed PoolManager. Features that only exist after 8 December (Jenner CAS20, Tempo T14) go through a time override where the endpoint honours it, and are otherwise recorded as untestable until the day. Task 4: write the table into your result: network, feature, what the account controls, effect on sync and settle, effect on take, evidence. Any row where an ordinary account gains a credit it did not pay for, or makes another account's settle or take fail, is a finding with actor unprivileged; say whose funds and how much. If every row is nothing or a revert, record the rows as cleared with their evidence and list the rows still resting on reading.

code.title: Tempo: whether anything a contract can call on the main branch and at T15 starts a transaction inside a running one
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 34 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Lead L-1274. Tempo's interpreter (evm2 7c9f3b6d on v1.19.2, e80df9c4 on reth main) supports a transaction dispatched from inside a running one. It shares the single State, so when the inner transaction ends, the transient storage of the outer one is cleared. Cycle 34 read what that does to an open PoolManager unlock: the lock slot, the count of open deltas, every delta and the synced currency read zero afterwards (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32, CurrencyDelta.sol:21-41, CurrencyReserves.sol). A caller could take a currency, trigger the nested transaction and reach the end of unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) with its debt erased, which takes pooled funds of every pool. Cycles 33 and 34 cleared this because no production code calls that path at c0c9372 or on main today. T14 activates on 8 December 2026 and T15 is targeted for 15 December with a release that does not exist yet; Tempo has one client, so whatever that release contains is the network. This theme reads what is being built for it. Comparing revisions of Tempo and evm2 is allowed and wanted. Scripts: research/network-risk/cycles/034/theme-evm2-main-native-run.work/scripts (callers.py, crawl.py), research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-tempo-v1192-nested-dispatch.work/scripts (callers.py, crawl.py, tprobe.py) and research/network-risk/cycles/019/theme-tempo-nested-exec.work (tprobe.py, tcarry.py). Task 1: fetch tempo main and every branch or open pull request head that the repository shows for T15, zones, subblocks or TIP-20 routing (raw.githubusercontent.com and the public git protocol; do not work around a refusal). Record commit hashes and dates. List every file added or changed since c0c9372 under crates/precompiles, the transaction handler, the payload builder and the evm wrapper. Task 2: rerun callers.py on each tree and list every non-test caller of transact, call_tx, system_call, execute_system_call, committed_copy, execute_tx and any new function that builds a transaction environment and runs it. For each caller trace upward to its entry: a block-level hook (before the first or after the last user transaction), the transaction handler before or after execution, or a precompile or host call that a contract can reach with CALL. Read in particular the TIP-20 route to zone portals (crates/precompiles/src/tip20: resolve_transfer, deposit_virtual and whatever they call), fee token conversion, the 0x76 batch type, keychain and sub-account calls, and any zone or subblock code: is each a call frame on the same journal, or a dispatched transaction? Task 3: for every path that a contract can reach, say whether a hook, a token or an unlock callback on Tempo can reach it while the PoolManager is unlocked, and what the outer frame then reads from the lock slot, the count, its delta and the synced currency. Test what the live build has by eth_simulateV1 on rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz with state overrides at current and T14 rules (tprobe.py pattern: open an unlock and a delta, sync a currency, call the path, read the four with exttload before and after), bracketed by web3_clientVersion. Task 4: read how the transaction handler itself uses transient storage across the phases of one user transaction (fee collection, the batch of calls of a 0x76 transaction, refund settlement): is transient storage cleared between the calls of one batch transaction, or only at its end? A PoolManager unlock opened in one call of a batch cannot stay open into the next call, but a sync can (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288): say what a later call of the same batch, by the same account, reads. Task 5: write down the exact check to rerun on the day a T15 tag appears (the caller list, the paths, the live probe). A path within an ordinary account's reach that clears or shares transient storage under an open unlock, on any tree that is tagged for release, is a finding with actor unprivileged; on an untagged branch it is a high-priority lead with the commit. If no such path exists, record trees, callers and probes as cleared. This theme concerns Tempo only; say so for the other 20 networks.
